body.statement: If the independently specified oracle-instance \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}=(x_{\mathrm{str}},\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}})\) is feasible, then the minimum defining \(\operatorname{Opt}\) is attained by the lexicographically first canonical uniform certificate \(E^{\star}\). Exhaustive enumeration of certificates of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\), with cached oracle replies, outputs \(E^{\star}\), its protocol masks, exact \(|\mathrm{LIT}|\)-bit slice labels, source masks, factor-ownership masks, and one uniform finite restriction transcript schema per factor. Its time is \(2^{O(B_{\mathrm{cert}})}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{E^{\star}}+N_{\mathcal O})\), where \(N_{\mathcal O}\) charges every issued protocol query and returned law-handle and support-table bit. The verifier executes complete unconditional CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) on the decoded oracle-backed source collection. No bounded-treewidth runtime is claimed.
body.justification: The theorem retains exact cost optimization while exposing both the assignment-sensitive certificate size and every source-law or support access in the computational model.
body.gap: Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025), Theorem 1 on page 5 and Lemma 3 on page 8, reduce a connected ordinary \(Q[S]\) target to one intervention and a hedge-hitting problem; Lemma 7 on page 12 certifies their exact Algorithm 2, and Proposition 3 on page 16 certifies their general-target Algorithm 3. Those results optimize ordinary intervention sets under fixed \(Q[S]\) source-family semantics, not oracle-explicit SELECT-RAND-CTF-RAND-READ protocols with reusable counterfactual slices and branch-labelled certificates.
body.consumer: Park and Lee's counterfactual structural causal bandit can compare the exact acquisition prices of finite reward-law protocols without treating source support as free hidden input.
